- Season first: 2 becomes 4, then Scales makes it 5.

Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5), so it doesn't loop.

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now

Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
Their **Clone** is a regular Tarmogoyf. It doesn't get the counters or the Giant Growth bonus, but it has the same power/toughness ability, so it is always the same base size as your goyf.

Per `707.2`, a copy gets only the copiable values, meaning what's printed on the card (as changed by other copy effects). "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." Your two +1/+1 counters and **Giant Growth**'s +3/+3 stay on your creature only. Clone's own rulings say the same: it doesn't copy counters or "any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness".

The Clone still knows how big to be. Per `707.2a`, a copy gets the abilities of what it copies "because those values are derived from its rules text." **Tarmogoyf**'s */*+1 isn't a fixed number. It comes from its rules text: "Tarmogoyf's power is equal to the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1." The Clone copies that text, so it counts graveyards on its own, all the time.

One detail: Giant Growth went to the graveyard after it resolved. If no other instant was there already, it added a card type, so both goyfs grew by +1/+1. Example: with 3 card types in graveyards, the Clone is 3/4 and your goyf is 3/4 + 2 counters + 3 = 8/9 until end of turn.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer:
Either way, your non-enchantment creatures are still 1/1 with no abilities. **Opalescence** says "Each other non-Aura enchantment", so it never animates itself and stays an ordinary enchantment. The only thing the order changes is **Humility**'s own size.

**Humility out first, then Opalescence (your case):**
- Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a creature.
- Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility's effect removes all abilities from creatures, including its own. Per 613.6, though, once an effect has started applying, it keeps applying in later layers "even if the ability generating the effect is removed". So Humility's 1/1 part still happens.
- Layer 7b (613.4b): Both cards set P/T here, and they apply in timestamp order (613.7). Humility's earlier effect sets 1/1 first. Then Opalescence's later effect sets Humility to 4/4, because its mana value is 4.

Result: Humility is a 4/4 creature enchantment with no abilities, and it still makes every other creature 1/1. Opalescence isn't affected.

**Opalescence out first, then Humility:** Layers 4 and 6 work the same way. In 7b, Opalescence sets Humility to 4/4 first, and then Humility's later effect makes every creature 1/1. So Humility is a 1/1 with no abilities.

Any other non-Aura enchantments follow the same pattern as Humility. They have no abilities either way. They're 1/1 if Humility is newer, or P/T equal to their mana value if Opalescence is newer. The official ruling on these two cards confirms this.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer:
Yes, you can cast **Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor** straight from your hand for {5}{B}{R}. **Valki** is a modal double-faced card, so you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack (712.11b). It isn't a planeswalker card in your library, hand or graveyard, though. Outside the battlefield and stack it has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a). There it is a 2-mana-value legendary creature card named Valki.

On the battlefield, only the face that's up counts (712.8f). If Tibalt resolves, it's a planeswalker permanent, not a creature. **Vraska's Contempt** ("Exile target creature or planeswalker") and **Kaya's Ghostform** ("Enchant creature or planeswalker you control") only care about permanents on the battlefield, so what the card is in your library or graveyard doesn't matter to them. Both work on Tibalt, and both work on Valki.

One catch with Ghostform on Tibalt: if Tibalt dies or is exiled, Ghostform will "return that card to the battlefield under your control". A double-faced card put onto the battlefield from anywhere other than the stack enters front face up (712.14). So you get **Valki** back, not Tibalt. Valki's enters trigger then makes each opponent reveal their hand again, and you exile a creature card from each.

rows.question: melded my Bruna and Gisela into Brisela and then it got Path to Exiled. does that count as one creature leaving or two for my [[Blood Artist]] type triggers, and do I get one Plains or two off Path?

permanent is a single object represented by two cards (712.21, 701.42a). A trigger reading

Blood Artist's Oracle text reads "Whenever this creature or another creature dies, target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life." So it triggers once for itself and once for each other creature. rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? And separately, if I have two Ragavan on the battlefield somehow, when exactly does the legend rule kick in - can I respond in between?
rows.expected_answer: 1) It doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would receive priority, not in the middle of a spell resolving (704.3, 704.4 - the CR's own Maro example). The creature only dies if it still has toughness 0 or less when SBAs are next checked (704.5f). 2) The legend rule (704.5j) is also a state-based action: the moment a player would get priority with two Ragavans you control, you choose one and the other goes to the graveyard. It doesn't use the stack and there is no window to respond between the second Ragavan entering and the legend rule applying; you can only respond before the second one enters/resolves.

outcome.answer:
No, it doesn't die, as long as its toughness is back above 0 when the spell finishes resolving. As for the two **Ragavan**s: the legend rule applies before anyone gets priority, so you can't respond in between.

**The 0-toughness moment:** `704.4` says that state-based actions "pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability." The game only checks them when a player would get priority (`704.3`). The **Maro** ruling says the same thing: a creature is only put into the graveyard for 0 toughness "when state-based actions are checked." If its toughness drops to 0 mid-resolution and is back up (for example with **Giant Growth**'s +3/+3 still applying) by the time the spell finishes, it survives. If its toughness is still 0 or less at that check, it goes to the graveyard under `704.5f`.

**Two Ragavans:** The legend rule is a state-based action under `704.5j`. If you control two legendary permanents with the same name, you choose one and the other goes to its owner's graveyard. State-based actions don't use the stack (`704.1`) and are handled before any player would receive priority (`117.2d`). So once the second Ragavan resolves and enters, the game checks state-based actions and applies the legend rule before you or anyone else gets priority. Your only window is while the second Ragavan spell is still on the stack. After it resolves, you just pick which Ragavan to keep.

rows.question: I attack with a 5/5 trample that also has deathtouch (Questing Beast) and they block with a 4/4. how much can I trample over? my opponent says I have to assign 4 to the blocker first

Deathtouch changes what counts as lethal: per 702.2c, "any nonzero amount of combat damage assigned to a creature by a source with deathtouch is considered to be lethal damage." So 1 damage meets the lethal requirement, and the 4/4 is still destroyed by that 1 deathtouch damage (702.2b). You can put more on the blocker if you want, but you don't have to.

One caveat: **Questing Beast**'s current Oracle text gives it only "Vigilance, deathtouch, haste". It has no trample of its own, so this only works if something else is giving it trample. Without trample, a blocked creature puts all its damage on its blocker (510.1c).

rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?
rows.expected_answer: 1) Yes. Color identity includes mana symbols in the mana cost AND in the rules text (903.4), so Kenrith's identity is WUBRG even though his mana cost is only {4}{W}. Nicol Bolas, the Ravager (UBR) is legal because every color in its identity is in Kenrith's (903.5c). 2) Yes, Kenrith can go to the command zone. If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead - a replacement effect (903.9b). Graveyard/exile use a separate state-based action (903.9a). Either way it's optional.

outcome.answer:
1) Yes, you can run **Nicol Bolas, the Ravager**. 2) Yes, Kenrith can go to the command zone. Being sent to your hand or library counts too, not just the graveyard or exile, and it's your choice.

**Color identity:** Per `903.4`, a card's color identity includes the mana symbols in its rules text as well as its mana cost. **Kenrith, the Returned King** costs {4}{W}, and his abilities cost {R}, {G}, {W}, {U} and {B} ("{R}: All creatures gain trample and haste until end of turn." … "{4}{B}: Put target creature card from a graveyard…"). That makes his identity all five colors. Nicol Bolas's front face costs {1}{U}{B}{R}. Per `903.4d`, the back face also counts, but Nicol Bolas, the Arisen is only blue, black and red too. Per `903.5c`, a card is legal if every color in its identity is in your commander's identity, and blue, black and red all are.

**Unsummon:** **Unsummon** says "Return target creature to its owner's hand." Per `903.9b`, "If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead." This is a replacement, so Kenrith goes straight to the command zone and never touches your hand. Because it's optional, you can also let him go to your hand and recast him from there later. The graveyard/exile option you're thinking of is a separate rule, `903.9a`, which is a state-based action.

rows.question: commander damage question. I've been hit for 15 by my opponent's Rafiq. she then copies it with a Clone and hits me for 6 more with the clone. do I lose? also does the 21 count noncombat damage like from Fling?
rows.expected_answer: No to both. A player loses when they've been dealt 21 or more COMBAT damage by the SAME commander over the course of the game (903.10a; checked as a state-based action, 704.6c). The Clone copying Rafiq is not a commander, so its 6 damage isn't commander damage - you're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. Fling damage is noncombat, so it never counts toward the 21 either; it just reduces your life total normally.

outcome.answer:
No, you don't lose to commander damage. You've taken 15 from her commander. The other 6 came from a creature that isn't a commander, and Fling damage never counts toward the 21.

The Clone isn't a commander. Being a commander is "an attribute of the card itself", not a characteristic that copy effects can copy. `903.3` says it directly: "A permanent that’s copying a commander ... is not a commander." So the **Clone** copying **Rafiq of the Many** is a separate source.

The loss condition in `903.10a` needs 21 or more combat damage "by the same commander." You're at 15 from Rafiq. If the real Rafiq hits you for 6 more combat damage later, that does reach 21 and you lose.

Noncombat damage doesn't count either, because `903.10a` only counts combat damage. On top of that, **Fling** is the source of its own damage: "Fling deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to any target." That's true even if she sacrifices Rafiq itself to pay for it. So it adds nothing to the commander damage count.

All of that damage still makes you lose life normally (`119.2`). Starting from 40, the 15 plus 6 puts you at 19, not counting anything else that hit you. Any further damage, including Fling, keeps lowering your life total, and you lose if it reaches 0.

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?
rows.expected_answer: 1) No. Each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana added during your upkeep is lost before your main phase (106.4). Tap the lands in your main phase instead. 2) Yes. Casting a spell includes a step where, if the total cost includes mana, you get a chance to activate mana abilities such as tapping lands (601.2g), and only then do you pay the total cost (601.2h). You do not need to float mana before announcing the spell.

outcome.answer:
1) No. Mana you add during your upkeep is gone before your main phase. 2) Yes, you can tap lands partway through casting **Snapcaster Mage**. You don't need to float the mana first.

**Upkeep mana:** Per `106.4`, each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase. Upkeep is a step of the beginning phase (`501.1`), so that mana empties at the end of upkeep. It also couldn't survive the draw step after that. To cast **Jace, the Mind Sculptor** in your main phase, tap your lands during that main phase.

**Tapping while casting:** Casting a spell has its own window for this. Per `601.2g`, once the total cost is set, you get a chance to activate mana abilities, and you do this before you pay the costs. `605.3a` says you can activate a mana ability while you're casting a spell that needs a mana payment. Tapping a land for mana is a mana ability (`106.12`). So the normal sequence is: put Snapcaster on the stack, work out the cost, tap your lands, then pay. Floating mana first also works, but you never have to.

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
rows.expected_answer: No copy. Academy Manufactor's "instead" makes it a replacement effect (614.1a), and Shelob's trigger would create a Food token, so Manufactor applies. The replaced event never happens (614.6): instead of the Food that would be a copy of the creature, you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure token. Those are predefined tokens with only their standard characteristics (111.10a, 111.10b, 111.10f). 111.10 lets the effect that creates a predefined token modify it, but Shelob's modifications belonged to the replaced event, and Manufactor's own effect modifies nothing. outcome.answer:
Neither. You don't get the Food copy at all. **Academy Manufactor** replaces the copy, and you get one plain Food, one plain Clue and one plain Treasure instead.

Shelob's trigger says to "create a token that's a copy of that creature, except it's a Food artifact". That's an instruction to create a Food token, so Manufactor applies: "If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each." Because the effect uses "instead", it's a replacement effect (614.1a). Per 614.6, a replaced event never happens. The copy token is never created. Manufactor's new event happens in its place, and it creates one Clue, one Food and one Treasure.

You lose the creature's abilities and any enters-the-battlefield triggers it would have had. "One of each" also doesn't mean you keep the original token and add the other two.

If you'd rather have the Food copy, you can't opt out. Manufactor's effect isn't optional.
